categories.main_business_segments: Coca-Cola Consolidated is the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the United States, operating primarily through its Nonalcoholic Beverages segment. The company distributes, markets, and manufactures nonalcoholic beverages across 14 states and the District of Columbia, serving approximately 60 million consumers. Approximately 85% of bottle/can sales consist of The Coca-Cola Company products, with the remainder from other beverage companies including Keurig Dr Pepper and Monster Energy.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company operates 10 manufacturing plants utilizing standard beverage production and packaging technologies for both sparkling and still beverages. Production methods include concentrate mixing, carbonation, bottling in plastic and aluminum cans, and post-mix syrup dispensing systems. The company also participates in South Atlantic Canners, a manufacturing cooperative, and co-owns plastic bottle and aluminum can suppliers (Southeastern Container and Western Container).
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company serves grocery stores, mass merchandise stores, club stores, convenience stores, drug stores, on-premise locations (restaurants, schools, amusement parks), and vending machine outlets. Major customers include Walmart (21% of bottle/can volume) and The Kroger Company (14% of bottle/can volume), together representing 35% of total bottle/can sales volume. The company operates across five principal markets: Carolinas, Central, Mid-Atlantic, Mid-South, and Mid-West regions.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates in 14 U.S. states and the District of Columbia, organized into five principal markets: Carolinas (North Carolina, South Carolina, southern Virginia), Central (Kentucky, West Virginia, southern Ohio, southeastern Indiana, southwestern Pennsylvania), Mid-Atlantic (Maryland, Virginia, Delaware, District of Columbia, south-central Pennsylvania), Mid-South (Arkansas, Tennessee, western Kentucky, northwestern Mississippi), and Mid-West (Indiana, Ohio, southeastern Illinois).
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates as a midstream bottler and distributor in the beverage supply chain. It manufactures products at 10 plants, distributes through 60 distribution centers using company-owned vehicles and warehouses, and increasingly uses alternative distribution methods. The company purchases concentrates from The Coca-Cola Company and finished products from other manufacturers, then sells to retail customers and on-premise locations.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Key strategic priorities include commercial execution, revenue management through optimal pricing, supply chain optimization with consolidation and automation investments, cash flow generation, optimal route-to-market implementation, and development of a digitally enabled selling platform (MyCoke 360) through CONA. The company is investing significantly in capital expenditures for supply chain modernization and future growth, with anticipated 2024 spending of $300-350 million.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through bottle/can sales (91% of net sales in 2023) of sparkling and still beverages sold to retail and on-premise customers. Additional revenue comes from sales to other Coca-Cola bottlers, post-mix sales, transportation services, and equipment maintenance. Revenue is recognized at point of sale upon delivery for bottle/can and post-mix sales, and over time for service revenues.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: The company competes in the highly competitive nonalcoholic beverage industry against local bottlers of PepsiCo products and regional Dr Pepper bottlers, as well as private label beverage producers. As the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the United States, the company competes primarily on brand strength, product quality, pricing, point-of-sale merchandising, customer service, distribution frequency, and advertising support from brand companies.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: The company is a large accelerated filer with 2023 net sales of $6.65 billion, representing 7.3% growth from 2022 ($6.20 billion). Net income was $408.4 million in 2023 compared to $430.2 million in 2022. The company has approximately 17,000 employees and generated $810.7 million in operating cash flow in 2023. Total assets reached $4.29 billion as of December 31, 2023, with long-term debt of $599.2 million.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: The company emphasizes strong execution of commercial strategy, optimal pricing and revenue management, supply chain efficiency, and customer service excellence. Key differentiators include exclusive distribution rights in assigned territories, a diverse portfolio of leading brands (Coca-Cola, Sprite, Fanta, Monster Energy, BODYARMOR, glacéau smartwater), investments in digital selling platforms, and commitment to community engagement through charitable giving programs totaling approximately $49 million in 2023.
